q: How large a quantity of heat is needed when $2.0\,\text{kg}$ of water is heated from $15\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ to $65\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ ($c = 4190\,\tfrac{\text{J}}{\text{kg}\cdot\text{K}}$)?
A kilogram of water and a kilogram of iron receive the same quantity of heat in a sauna. Whose temperature rises more, and about how many times as much?
a: The iron's. Its specific heat capacity, $450\,\text{J/(kg}\cdot\text{K)}$, is about one ninth of that of water, $4190\,\text{J/(kg}\cdot\text{K)}$, so the same quantity of heat raises the temperature of the iron about nine times as much.
